notes.written: 2026-10-25 (UTC), for the codus-copy jargon engine (check-jargon.mjs). The engine reads jargon, coined, allowedAnywhere, allowedLines and concrete; it ignores this notes object, which records why each entry is here.
notes.terminology: Project rule #52: in anything a visitor reads, a limit with its own reset is a 'window', it 'resets', and what Claude Code and the Codex CLI keep is a 'sign-in'. Never 'quota', 'auth' or 'credential'. The jargon list enforces the never-words and their relatives; 'quota' and 'quotas' are whole-word rules so the brand name QuotaDial and the domain quotadial.com never trip them.
notes.coined: None yet. A coined word must be glossed in plain words at first use, and the engine reports coined words for a person to check by eye; it never fails a page on them.

allowedAnywhereReasons.API: QuotaDial ships a local HTTP API on 127.0.0.1; developers search for it and call it by this name.
allowedAnywhereReasons.MCP: The MCP server is how agents read the numbers; agent builders look for 'MCP server' by name.
allowedAnywhereReasons.CLI: Part of the product name 'Codex CLI', which every visitor in the audience runs daily.
allowedAnywhereReasons.macOS: An operating system's name; the download page is sorted by system.
allowedAnywhereReasons.Windows: An operating system's name; the download page is sorted by system.
allowedAnywhereReasons.Linux: An operating system's name; the download page is sorted by system.
allowedAnywhereReasons.Claude Code: The name of the tool whose sign-in QuotaDial reads.
allowedAnywhereReasons.Codex: The name of the tool whose sign-in QuotaDial reads.
allowedAnywhereReasons.GitHub: Where the downloads, the source and the issues live.
allowedAnywhereReasons.JSON: The command's --json output and the API's answers are JSON; developers expect the word. JSONL stays on the jargon list: the boundary guard keeps this allowance from blanking it.
allowedAnywhereReasons.SHA-256: Each release lists every file's SHA-256, and the check step names the algorithm the reader's own command uses.
allowedAnywhereReasons.webhook: Pro sends alerts to webhooks the reader adds; the audience writes webhooks and the setting is named for them, and any plain alternative would be longer and harder to find. Kept for a developer audience; re-argue it if the audience widens. Its plural is plain text no jargon rule matches.

notes.keptOffTheList: 'cache' and 'fetched' are the app's own words for where a number came from and when (crates/core/src/text.rs source_label: 'the API', 'local logs', 'cache'; doctor output 'fetched 3 min ago'), and #52 asks for the same words in the app, the command and the site. Flagging them here would fail the site for quoting the app faithfully. 'webhook' is allowed above for the same audience reason.
notes.verbatimRenders: Decided 2026-10-25: /privacy and /changelog show docs/PRIVACY.md (D-106) and CHANGELOG.md (D-101) word for word, because each is the product's one text, also shown in the app and the README, and its own words (token, daemon, poller) are accurate there. allowedLines holds exactly the lines of those renders that this list flags, as the engine splits the built pages (a code element is dropped to a space, and the files' own line breaks split lines). The site's own words around them follow this list. When either file changes, build the site, run the engine on out/privacy.html and out/changelog.html, and replace these lines with the ones it reports from the renders; never add a line the site wrote itself.
notes.selftest: Run JARGON_CONFIG=<this file> node ~/.claude/skills/codus-copy/scripts/check-jargon.mjs --selftest. It plants every jargon term, a code-mock control, the beside-line control (the first allowed token, API, beside the first jargon term, quota) and the engine's own boundary probes.
